lead: AWS's entry cert. It proves you can explain what the AWS Cloud is, who secures what, which core service does which job, and how AWS charges for it. No hands-on work is required. It's a good first cloud cert before Solutions Architect, and it teaches you the words cloud teams and contractors use every day.
objSub: Four domains and 19 task statements from AWS's CLF-C02 exam guide. Tick them off as you study; progress saves on this device.

c02.label: C02
c02.note: The only version on sale. AWS hasn't announced a CLF-C03. AWS posts exam guide changes about a month before they reach the exam, so check the exam page before you book.
c02.onote: Official AWS task statements (CLF-C02 exam guide), in plain words. Weights are AWS's share of scored content.

domains.name: Cloud Concepts
obj: Benefits of the AWS Cloud
Pay only for what you use, AWS's lower prices from huge scale, speed and agility, going global in minutes, high availability and elasticity, and no more guessing how much hardware to buy.
Design principles
The six pillars of the Well-Architected Framework: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization and sustainability.
Migration benefits and strategies

The Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) and its perspectives; migration strategies such as rehost (lift and shift), replatform, refactor, repurchase, retain and retire; tools like the Snow Family and Database Migration Service.
Cloud economics

Fixed vs variable cost; on-premises costs you stop paying, like power, cooling and hardware refresh; licensing (bring your own vs included); right-sizing; the value of managed services and automation.

domains.name: Security and Compliance
obj: The shared responsibility model

AWS secures the cloud itself: buildings, hardware, the network and the services' software. You secure what you put in it: your data, IAM, security groups and, on EC2, the operating system. The split shifts by service (EC2 vs RDS vs Lambda).
Security, governance and compliance concepts
Where AWS's compliance reports live (AWS Artifact); encryption at rest and in transit; audit and governance tools like CloudTrail, Config, CloudWatch and Audit Manager.
Access management

IAM users, groups, roles and policies; least privilege; lock down the root user with MFA and don't use it day to day; IAM Identity Center for single sign-on; access keys vs passwords; Secrets Manager.
Security components and resources
Security groups, network ACLs, AWS WAF, Shield, GuardDuty, Inspector, Security Hub and Detective; Trusted Advisor checks; AWS Marketplace security tools; security blogs and the Knowledge Center.

domains.name: Cloud Technology and Services
obj: Deploying and operating
Console, CLI, SDKs and APIs; infrastructure as code with CloudFormation; cloud, hybrid and on-premises deployment models; connecting with Site-to-Site VPN or Direct Connect.
Global infrastructure
Regions, Availability Zones and edge locations; why two or more AZs give high availability; picking a Region for law, latency, cost and the services you need.
Compute services
EC2 and its instance families, Auto Scaling and Elastic Load Balancing; containers with ECS, EKS and Fargate; serverless with Lambda; Elastic Beanstalk.
Database services
RDS and Aurora (relational), DynamoDB (NoSQL key-value), ElastiCache (in-memory), Neptune (graph); managed databases vs installing your own on EC2; the Database Migration Service.
Network services
VPC, public and private subnets, route tables, internet and NAT gateways; security groups vs network ACLs; Route 53 (DNS); CloudFront and Global Accelerator; VPN and Direct Connect.
Storage services
S3 and its storage classes and lifecycle rules; EBS volumes for EC2; EFS shared file storage; FSx; Storage Gateway for hybrid; AWS Backup.
AI/ML and analytics services
What SageMaker AI, Bedrock, Rekognition, Comprehend, Lex, Polly and Textract do; analytics with Athena, Kinesis, Glue, Redshift, EMR and QuickSight.
Other service categories
Messaging (SQS, SNS, EventBridge), developer tools (CodeBuild, CodePipeline), end-user computing (WorkSpaces), web and mobile front ends (Amplify), IoT Core and Amazon Connect.

domains.name: Billing, Pricing, and Support
obj: Pricing models
On-Demand, Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, Spot Instances, Dedicated Hosts and Dedicated Instances; data coming in is free, data going out costs; storage tiers.
Billing, budget and cost tools
Billing console, AWS Budgets, Cost Explorer, the Cost and Usage Report and the Pricing Calculator; consolidated billing in AWS Organizations; cost allocation tags.
Technical resources and Support
AWS Support plans and what each adds; technical account managers; Trusted Advisor; AWS Health Dashboard; re:Post, the Knowledge Center and Prescriptive Guidance; AWS Partners and Marketplace.

extras.title: Global infrastructure
rows: A separate geographic area with 3+ AZs. Pick it for law, latency, cost and services
One or more data centers with their own power and network. Spread apps across 2+
CloudFront and Route 53 serve users from here, close to them
AWS compute placed close to a big city for low latency
AWS racks installed in your own data center

extras.title: Pricing models
rows: No commitment. Short, spiky or unknown workloads
Commit to an hourly spend; flexible across instance types
Commit to an instance type; steady workloads
Up to 90% off, but AWS can take it back with a 2-minute warning
Per-socket licenses or rules that need your own hardware

extras.title: Lock down a new account
rows: Turn on MFA for the root user. Don't create root access keys.
Create admin access through IAM Identity Center (or an IAM role), and stop using root.
Create a CloudTrail trail so API history is kept longer than the 90-day default.
Set an AWS Budgets alert before you launch anything.
Turn on GuardDuty and look at Trusted Advisor's security checks.

extras.title: Support plans
rows: Docs, re:Post, the Health Dashboard and core Trusted Advisor checks
24/7 cases; AWS aims to answer critical issues within 30 minutes
Adds a technical account manager; 15 minutes for critical issues
A designated AWS team; 5 minutes for critical issues
Developer, Business and Enterprise On-Ramp. The CLF-C02 guide still uses these names

method: Use the four domains above as your checklist. Security and the technology domain are almost two-thirds of the exam.
Take AWS's free Cloud Practitioner Essentials course on Skill Builder, or one video course. Don't buy three.
Open a personal Free Tier account, set a budget alert first, then launch an EC2 instance, an S3 bucket and an IAM role. Delete them after.
Flashcards: one card per service with what it does in one line. Many questions are just “which service does this?”
Take AWS's free official practice question set, then timed practice exams. Review every miss.
tips: “Managed,” “serverless” and “least effort” point to the AWS service that runs it for you, not EC2.
For shared responsibility questions, ask: can I touch it? If you can configure it, it's yours.
Multiple response questions tell you how many to pick. No partial credit, so check you picked exactly that many.
This is a breadth exam. If an answer needs deep design trade-offs, it's probably a distractor.

quiz.q: A review finds your team patches servers by hand, has no runbooks, and learns about outages when users call. Which Well-Architected pillar needs the most work?
o: Operational excellence
Right. Running and monitoring systems, automating changes and writing runbooks are operational excellence.
Reliability
Reliability is about recovering from failure and scaling to demand. The findings here are about how the team operates.
Security
Patching touches security, but runbooks and monitoring are operations problems.
Performance efficiency
That pillar is about picking the right resource types and sizes.

quiz.q: A data center is closing in 60 days. The team copies its servers onto EC2 as they are, with no code changes. Which migration strategy is this?
o: Rehost
Right. Rehost, or lift and shift, moves the servers as they are. It's the fastest way out of a data center.
Replatform
Replatform makes small changes on the way, like moving the database to RDS.
Refactor
Refactor rebuilds the app for the cloud, like going serverless. That takes far longer than 60 days.
Repurchase
Repurchase replaces the app with a SaaS product.

quiz.q: Your unit moves its file server from a closet server room to AWS. Which cost does the unit STOP paying directly?
o: Power and cooling for the server room
Right. AWS pays for power, cooling and hardware. That's built into its prices.
Licenses for software you bring yourself
With bring-your-own-license, you still pay for those licenses.
Staff time to manage users and permissions
IAM and access are still your job under shared responsibility.
Data sent from AWS out to users
That's a new cost. Data out of AWS is billed.

quiz.q: Your unit runs a database on Amazon RDS. Which task is YOUR responsibility?
o: Controlling who can connect, with security groups and database users
Right. Network access and accounts are always the customer's job.
Patching the operating system under the database
RDS is managed. AWS patches the OS and the database engine in your maintenance window.
Replacing a failed disk in the server
Hardware is always AWS's job.
Guarding the data center doors
Physical security is always AWS's job.

quiz.q: An auditor asks for AWS's own SOC 2 and ISO 27001 reports. Where do you download them?
o: AWS Artifact
Right. Artifact is the self-service portal for AWS's compliance reports and agreements.
AWS Audit Manager
Audit Manager collects evidence about YOUR account. It doesn't hold AWS's reports.
AWS Config
Config records how your resources are set up over time.
AWS Trusted Advisor
Trusted Advisor checks your account against best practices.

quiz.q: A script on an EC2 instance must read files from an S3 bucket. What's the MOST secure way to give it access?
o: Attach an IAM role to the instance with read access to that bucket
Right. The role hands the instance temporary credentials that rotate on their own. No keys to leak.
Put an IAM user's access keys in the script
Long-lived keys in a file get copied, committed to Git and leaked.
Use the root user's access keys
Root should never have access keys, let alone in a script.
Make the bucket public
That exposes the files to the whole internet.

quiz.q: Which service watches CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs and alerts on threats like crypto-mining or calls from known bad IP addresses?
o: Amazon GuardDuty
Right. GuardDuty is AWS's managed threat detection service.
Amazon Inspector
Inspector scans EC2, container images and Lambda for software vulnerabilities.
Amazon Macie
Macie finds sensitive data, like PII, in S3.
AWS Shield
Shield protects against DDoS attacks.

quiz.q: A training portal must keep running if one data center loses power. What meets this with the LEAST effort?
o: Run it on instances in two or more Availability Zones behind a load balancer
Right. Each AZ has its own power and network, so losing one doesn't take the app down.
Run it on two instances in the same Availability Zone
One AZ can fail as a whole. Both copies would go down.
Move it to a bigger instance
A bigger server is still one server in one place.
Back it up to S3 every night
Backups help you recover later. They don't keep the app running.

quiz.q: A function resizes each photo when it's uploaded. It runs for 2 seconds, a few hundred times a day. Which option costs least and needs no servers to manage?
o: AWS Lambda
Right. You pay only for the milliseconds it runs, and there's no server to patch.
An EC2 On-Demand instance running all day
You'd pay for 24 hours to do a few minutes of work.
An EC2 Spot Instance
Cheaper than On-Demand, but still a server you manage, and it can be taken back.
Amazon ECS on EC2
Containers on EC2 still leave you managing the instances.

quiz.q: Several Linux EC2 instances in different Availability Zones must read and write the same files at the same time. Which storage fits?
o: Amazon EFS
Right. EFS is a shared file system that many instances can mount across AZs.
Amazon EBS
An EBS volume lives in one AZ and normally attaches to one instance.
Instance store
It's tied to one instance and is wiped when the instance stops.
S3 Glacier Deep Archive
An archive class. Getting data back takes hours.

quiz.q: Which statement about security groups and network ACLs is TRUE?
o: Security groups are stateful and protect instances; network ACLs are stateless and protect subnets
Right. A security group remembers the connection, so return traffic is allowed automatically. A NACL checks each direction on its own.
Security groups are stateless and protect subnets; network ACLs are stateful and protect instances
That's reversed.
Both can have deny rules
Only NACLs can deny. Security groups have allow rules only.
Network ACLs replace security groups
They work together as two layers.

quiz.q: An app stores user sessions as key-value pairs and needs single-digit millisecond reads at any scale, with no servers to manage. Which database?
o: Amazon DynamoDB
Right. DynamoDB is AWS's serverless NoSQL key-value database.
Amazon RDS for MySQL
A relational database on instances you size and scale.
Amazon Redshift
A data warehouse for analytics on large data sets.
Amazon Neptune
A graph database for relationships, like who knows whom.

quiz.q: A nightly batch job can be stopped and restarted at any time without harm. Which EC2 pricing option is cheapest?
o: Spot Instances
Right. Spot uses spare capacity at a big discount. Work that can be interrupted is the perfect fit.
Reserved Instances
Reservations suit steady, always-on workloads for 1 or 3 years.
On-Demand
It works, but it's the full price.
Dedicated Hosts
The most expensive option. It's for licensing or compliance needs.

quiz.q: The CO wants an email when the unit's AWS bill is FORECAST to pass $500 this month. Which tool?
o: AWS Budgets
Right. Budgets can alert on actual or forecasted spend.
AWS Cost Explorer
Cost Explorer charts and forecasts costs, but the alert is set up in Budgets.
AWS Pricing Calculator
It estimates costs before you build. It doesn't watch your bill.
AWS Cost and Usage Report
A detailed billing data file. It doesn't send alerts.

pbqs.title: Who's responsible?
pbqs.scenario: Your unit runs workloads on EC2, RDS and S3. For each task, pick who is responsible under the shared responsibility model.

rows.req: Patch the operating system on an EC2 instance
rows.why: On EC2 you control the OS, so patching it is yours.

rows.req: Patch the database engine on Amazon RDS
rows.why: RDS is managed. AWS patches the engine and the OS under it.

rows.req: Replace a failed hard drive in an AWS data center
Turn on encryption for sensitive data in an S3 bucket
rows.why: AWS gives you the tools. Deciding to use them, and how, is yours.

rows.req: Set the inbound rules on a security group
rows.why: You configure security groups. If you can change it, you own it.

rows.req: Train people on security and patch management
rows.why: These are shared controls: AWS trains its staff and patches its side; you train yours and patch your side.

pbqs.title: Pick the service
pbqs.scenario: Each request came from your division chief. Pick the AWS service that does it. Each answer is used once; four are distractors.

items.text: Show who deleted the training bucket, and when.
items.why: CloudTrail records API calls: who, what, when and from where.

items.text: Alarm when a server's CPU stays above 90% for 10 minutes.
items.why: CloudWatch collects metrics and runs alarms.

items.text: Serve our training videos quickly to sailors around the world.
items.why: CloudFront caches content at edge locations close to users.

items.text: Point training.example.com at our app and fail over to a backup site.
items.why: Route 53 is AWS's DNS, with health checks and failover routing.

items.text: Keep 50 TB of log archives we rarely read, as cheaply as possible.
items.why: S3, with a Glacier storage class, is built for cheap long-term storage.

items.text: Run a PostgreSQL database with automatic backups, without patching it ourselves.
items.why: RDS is the managed relational database service.

pbqs.title: Pick the pricing model
pbqs.scenario: Five workloads are coming to AWS. Pick the cheapest EC2 pricing model that still fits each one.

rows.req: A web server that will run 24/7 for the next three years
rows.why: A 1 or 3 year commitment gives the biggest discount on steady, always-on use.

rows.req: A two-week test of a new app; nobody knows the load
rows.why: Short and unpredictable: pay as you go with no commitment.

rows.req: Rendering jobs that can be interrupted and picked up later
rows.why: Interruptible work is what Spot is for.

rows.req: Software licensed per physical CPU socket
rows.why: A Dedicated Host gives you a whole physical server so you can use per-socket licenses.

rows.req: Extra capacity for a one-week exercise that must not be interrupted
rows.why: Too short for a commitment, and it can't risk Spot interruptions.

keep.text: Recertify by passing the latest Cloud Practitioner exam, by passing any Associate or Professional AWS exam, or for free with AWS Cloud Quest: Recertify Cloud Practitioner.
keep.after: The free Cloud Quest option opens in the last 6 months before it expires, and your cert must still be active. Each AWS exam you pass gives you a 50% discount voucher for your next one.

keep.text: No AWS cert is on the DoD 8140 matrix (V3.0). For a coded billet, you still need a cert that is, like Security+ or Cloud+.
keep.after: Cloud Practitioner is still useful: it's a cheap way to learn AWS before Solutions Architect.
